title: CI Rain
summary: Rain confidence intervals from sample after sample and count how many capture the true mean. Then do it with t.test() and replicate().
hints: Inside `replicate()`, put the steps in braces: draw `x`, get `ci <- t.test(x)$conf.int`, and end with `ci[1] <= 40 & 40 <= ci[2]`.
`mean(captured)` turns 1,000 TRUE/FALSE values into the proportion captured.

goals.text: Rain at least **100 intervals** at **95%** with **n = 10**.
goals.detail: Count the red ones. About 5 in 100 miss μ, and nothing about a single interval tells you whether it's one of them.

goals.text: Switch to **99%** and rain at least 100 more.
goals.detail: Fewer misses, but every interval is wider. More confidence costs precision.

goals.text: Back at 95%, make the intervals **narrower than 2 years** on average (at least 50 intervals).
goals.detail: Width shrinks with √n: to halve it you need four times the sample.

goals.text: Rain at least **1,000 intervals** at 95% and read the coverage.
goals.detail: The 95% is a property of the *method*: in the long run, about 95% of intervals made this way capture μ.
